writeup: TIC 334215307 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.4337 days. Data from NASA's TESS mission shows the primary eclipse causes a 4.27 percent dip in brightness, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 207.9 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal's origin near the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 38.1, though the centroid offset of 2.9 arcseconds leaves some uncertainty about the exact source. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially new object. The automated pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned it a score of 0.35, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing binary rather than an instrumental artifact.
